articles.title: In September 1983, a Soviet lieutenant colonel named Stanislav Petrov sat in a bunker south of Moscow watching his early-warning screens light up with five incoming American missiles, and instead of phoning it up the chain he decided the computer was lying and waited — a judgment call that historians now credit with preventing a retaliatory nuclear launch
articles.summary: On September 26, 1983, an alarm blared at the Serpukhov-15 bunker near Moscow, triggered by the Soviet Oko early-warning satellite system reporting incoming missiles. This critical moment, known as the 1983 Soviet nuclear false alarm incident, saw a Soviet officer, Stanislav Petrov, defy protocol and determine the launch warnings were erroneous, averting potential nuclear war through crucial human judgment.

articles.title: The Tense Discussions Behind Ronald Reagan’s ‘Tear Down This Wall’ Speech
